Wyld in NYC

Wyld is the Oregon-founded gummy brand produced under license in New York, and one of the most recognized edible names in the country. It is carried at 58 of the 67 licensed dispensaries we track, with about 530 products, all of them edibles. The line is simple: fruit-flavored gummies named for real fruits like blood orange, sour apple, raspberry and marionberry, in 10-count packs at 10 milligrams per piece, with ratio versions that add CBD, CBN or CBC.

Prices start at $17.60, with most packs between $26 and $30 before tax. Sweetlife on the Upper East Side, Bud & Honey in Flatiron and The Travel Agency SoHo each list 15 Wyld products, the deepest runs in the city, with Verdi Chelsea, The Travel Agency Downtown Brooklyn and The Flowery East Village close behind at 14. Because almost every shop carries it, Wyld is the easiest brand to find on short notice and a good benchmark for comparing gummy prices across the city.

Wyld FAQ
What is the difference between Wyld and Good Tide?

Good Tide is Wyld's sister brand, made with solventless rosin rather than distillate. Wyld is the larger and cheaper line; Good Tide is carried at fewer shops and starts around $25. Both are 10-count gummy packs.

Which Wyld gummies are for sleep?

The ones labeled with CBN, often an indica-leaning flavor like elderberry. Wyld's 1:1 THC-to-CBD packs are the gentler daytime option. Check the ratio on the pack.

Is Wyld made in New York?

Yes. Wyld licenses its recipes to New York producers, so the gummies sold at licensed dispensaries here are made in the state, as the law requires.
